children: SoftBank Group Corp.’s credit risk surged above 500 basis points for the first time in about four years, raising the prospect of even higher funding costs as the company presses ahead with massive investments in artificial intelligence.

SoftBank’s five-year credit-default swap rose to 516 basis points as of 6:30 a.m. in Tokyo, the highest since October 2022, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The spread on a dollar bond it sold in September with a 9.75% coupon, the highest ever for one of its dollar notes, has widened about 40% since issuance to about 644 basis points.

The deterioration comes as the AI stock trade reverses, raising questions about the future valuation of OpenAI, in which SoftBank has invested $64.6 billion, and its ability to recoup that investment. Wider bond spreads could also make future issuance and refinancing more expensive.

“The broadening of the AI business isn’t going to change, but monetisation will take longer,” said Masahito Sugawara, a senior strategist at Daiwa Securities Co. For AI firms relying on future cash flows to repay debt, delays in monetisation could complicate refinancing and “lead investors to demand wider spreads,” he said.

SoftBank’s financial burden is already growing. Finance costs in the July-September quarter rose 2.6 times from a year earlier to ¥461.9 billion ($2.9 billion). It rose by about ¥9 trillion during the quarter.

S&P Global Ratings said this month that key metrics were approaching the tolerance limits for its rating on SoftBank. It estimated the loan-to-value ratio has risen above 30%, approaching its 35% threshold for considering a downgrade.

Anthropic PBC shares fell below their initial public offering price less than four sessions after their record-setting debut. OpenAI has ruled out an IPO this year, adding uncertainty over the eventual valuation and monetisation of SoftBank’s massive investment.

title: SoftBank credit risk tops 500 basis points as AI worries mount
